model_family: Paired Gaussian-copula latent factor model with normal log10-leptin and lognormal positive raw-scale endpoints

evidence_use.operator: arithmetic means and sample SDs on complete endpoint pairs
evidence_use.population: 44 completers aged 7-14 with simple obesity; before/after 3-month home diet/exercise program with professional follow-up; no randomized parallel arm; 43 glucose and triglyceride pairs.
evidence_use.measurement: units specified per endpoint; pediatric leptin already log10(pg/mL)
evidence_use.reason: Use every supplied endpoint mean and SD as an arithmetic marginal parameter, converting positive endpoint parameters to lognormal log-location and log-scale. Leptin remains on its supplied log10 scale. Rounded complete-pair sample moments are plug-in reconstruction inputs, not known population parameters or independent validation evidence. Joint dependence is unidentified; finite synthetic sample moments may fluctuate.

evidence_use.population: 44 completers aged 7-14 with simple obesity; before/after 3-month home diet/exercise program with professional follow-up; no randomized parallel arm; 43 glucose and triglyceride pairs.
evidence_use.reason: Generate one row per completer with pre/post measurements and no parallel arm. Scale endpoint complete-pair counts as round(source_count*n/44), preserving 44 leptin/body-mass pairs and 43 glucose/triglyceride pairs at n=44. Both unavailable pairs occupy the final synthetic row by schema convention. Both-null fields and their co-placement do not establish native missingness. Eligibility is cohort-level provenance; age is not an output field and no unprovided age distribution is invented.

components.name: arithmetic marginal reconstruction
components.source_to_target_assumptions: Rounded complete-pair moments parameterize same-population rehearsal marginals. Normal applies directly to log10 leptin. For lognormal endpoints, log_variance=log(1+(sd/mean)^2) and log_mean=log(mean)-log_variance/2. No finite-sample recentering, rank optimization or fitted change statistic.

components.name: paired and cross-endpoint latent factors
components.source_to_target_assumptions: Independent standard-normal components have variance fractions shared stable person=0.20, stable endpoint=0.50, shared visit=0.05, endpoint-visit residual=0.25. Stable components persist across visits. Visit factors are independent across visits and shared across endpoints. Thus latent within-endpoint pre/post correlation is 0.70, same-visit cross-endpoint correlation is 0.25, and opposite-visit cross-endpoint correlation is 0.20. These are unestimated choices, selected before diagnostics. Nonlinear marginals alter observed correlations.

components.name: pair support and synthetic identity
components.source_to_target_assumptions: Unique generated identifiers, n persons, schema column order, and paired-null trailing rows with observed counts scaled from the packet. Trailing placement is independent of generated values and solely a storage convention. Positive endpoints use positive lognormal support without additional unprovided truncation bounds.

scenarios.assumption: One factor structure uses latent variance shares 0.20 stable person, 0.50 stable endpoint, 0.05 shared visit, and 0.25 residual. Common shares apply to all endpoints and visits. Source plug-in marginal moments are used without target joint information.
scenarios.inclusion_rationale: Stable person and endpoint components allow persistent paired measurements; a smaller shared visit factor permits coupled changes. This is one plausible executable completion of an unidentified joint distribution. Twenty cohorts allocate resources and are not posterior probability.
unresolved_dependencies: Actual within-person endpoint covariances are unavailable.
Actual cross-endpoint and cross-time covariances and change SDs/correlations are unavailable.
Gaussian copula and shared latent variance parameters are unverified.
Native missing-pair identities and mechanism are unavailable; schema-imposed co-missingness is not empirical evidence.
Uncertainty in rounded moment estimates and distribution-family approximation is not propagated.
affected_analysis_classes: Four paired endpoint change means with paired t intervals; input means are reconstruction inputs while finite-sample variation and interval width depend on assumed joint structure.

changes_from_parent: Initial build; no parent, scientific revision or examined alternative.

source_check_results.scope: Source-only contract and marginal diagnostic checks; no reserved outcomes or reference rows inspected.
source_check_results.interpretation: Envelope checks compare synthetic summaries to marginal reconstruction inputs. They do not validate assumed dependence, paired uncertainty or any clinical finding.

examined_structures.reason: Single factor-model structure selected from marginal distributions and paired design before numerical checking. All fixed seeds used without selection. No parameter changed after source checking.

calibration_log.execution_note: The initial diagnostic run completed all three seeds and decision validation, then JSON serialization failed on a NumPy boolean. The same unchanged three cohorts were deterministically replayed to serialize actual diagnostics. No additional unique cohort, structure, or scientific revision was examined.
calibration_log.selection_policy: One initial candidate; no target feedback, seed selection, alternative structure or parameter search.

intended_uses: Analysis-code rehearsal for paired endpoint summaries and change correlations.
Illustration of one explicitly assumed dependence completion.
unvalidated_uses: Causal treatment-effect estimation from this uncontrolled before/after design
Recovery of individual records, empirical dependence, native missingness or reserved target findings
Treating marginal source agreement as independent validation
next_information_request: Request a de-identified eight-variable pre/post covariance or correlation matrix with endpoint pair counts and overlap counts, stating raw versus log scale. Pre/post and cross-endpoint cross-time covariances would discriminate persistent-person versus shared-visit dependence without requesting test results or paper findings.
